newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Republicans recommend two for FCC posts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Republicans recommend two for FCC posts.

text.p: Senate Republican Leader Trent Lott said Thursday he had recommended Michael Powell and Harold Furchtgott-Roth to President Clinton as Republican members of the Federal Communications Commission.

Powell, chief of staff for the Justice Department's anti-trust division, is the son of retired Gen. Colin Powell, former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff at the Defense Department. Furchtgott-Roth is chief economist for the House Commerce Committee.
"Mr. Furchtgott-Roth and Mr. Powell bring the expertise the FCC so badly needs at this time," Lott said in a statement. "I hope the president will act expeditiously on them."
Clinton must formally send the nominations to the Senate for approval.
Sen. John McCain, an Arizona Republican, also endorsed the recommendations. He is chairman of the Commerce Committee, which would hold confirmation hearings on the nominees.
Terms of two of the five FCC commissioners have expired and the term of a third commissioner is due to end in June. No one party by law can have more than a 3-2 majority.
The commission regulates telecommunications and broadcasting. Its current chairman is Reed Hundt, a Democrat.
